facts.fact: StackAdapt's article cites an eMarketer figure that 53% of US marketers name social media as the top threat to their brand's reputation.
facts.quote: now naming social media as the top threat to their brand’s reputation

facts.fact: StackAdapt defines brand safety as protecting a brand's reputation by avoiding ad placements next to harmful or inappropriate content.
facts.quote: At its core, brand safety protects a brand’s reputation by avoiding ad placements next to harmful or inappropriate content.

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes brand suitability as focusing on positive alignment, choosing contexts that reinforce the brand message rather than just avoiding risk.
facts.quote: Suitability focuses on positive alignment, choosing contexts that reinforce the brand message rather than just avoiding risk.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that in pre-bid filtering, AI evaluates a page, app, or stream before an ad is placed and the bid is skipped if the environment is flagged as risky.
facts.quote: Before an ad is placed, AI can evaluate the content of the page, app, or stream. If the environment looks safe, the demand-side platform

facts.fact: StackAdapt claims its AI pre-bid filtering happens in milliseconds.
facts.quote: If it’s flagged as risky, the bid is skipped. This happens in milliseconds.

facts.fact: StackAdapt says that eight years before the page was written, its brand safety platform relied entirely on human reviewers to assess whether content was safe for advertisers.
facts.quote: Eight years ago, the platform relied entirely on human reviewers to assess whether content was safe for advertisers.
